correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and deterministic independent schedule, newest-vertex depth is nondecreasing and equals rooted height. The exact PGF depth recurrence is the continuant of a symmetric weighted path determinant. Bipartite sign symmetry gives an n-parity shifted r-factor Bernoulli PGF and compactness extends it to zero/one probabilities. Odd arrivals forced to immediate predecessor and arbitrary even-arrival choices realize every r-factor Bernoulli law. Discrete convex supporting lines and pairwise Bernoulli averaging yield two-sided bounds with explicit schedules achieving each endpoint; interpolation realizes all intermediate variances. The standalone Python exact-rational checker returned 67354 comparisons. Finite testing is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The finite-horizon height distribution is a natural invariant of temporally varying two-predecessor growth. The result completely classifies the feasible family (including its converse), then solves an exact non-asymptotic fixed-mean tree-design problem for all convex losses, not merely variance. Both extreme laws are realizable by transparent attachment schedules. This is not just a polynomial computation or a special value; it identifies the entire attainable shape of uncertainty and its sharp risk endpoints.
